body.statement: Benchmark normalization gives \(\pi_0(a\mid X)=b_a(X)\) almost surely for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and makes \(K(\theta)\ge0\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\). The regular optimizer path is continuously differentiable and satisfies \(H_c\theta_c'=-g_c\), \(\frac{d}{dc}K(\theta_c)=-g_c^\top H_c^{-1}g_c\le0\), and \(\frac{d}{dc}W(\theta_c)=c\frac{d}{dc}K(\theta_c)\). Under feature identification, either \(\theta_c=0\) for every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and the frontier is constant, or \(K(\theta_c)\) is strictly decreasing on \(\mathcal C\); thus a nonconstant maintained frontier has no self-intersection.
body.justification: This result prevents the proposal from manufacturing singular geometry that its own assumptions rule out.
body.gap: FangRidderXie2026 notes that restricted classes need not map preference one-to-one into divergence, but does not state this derivative characterization for the identifiable regular softmax path.
body.consumer: The result tells applied users when ordinary monotone interpolation is safe and when the constant-path set-valued report is necessary.
